clues: He was a prophet.
He was very old and his wife was barren.
He prayed quietly for a son.
He took care of Maryam in the sanctuary.
His son was Yahya.
easy.explain: Zakariyya called on his Lord in secret for an heir, and Allah gave him the good news of Yahya. He was also Maryam's guardian.

clues: He was a prophet.
He was given wisdom while still a child.
No one before him had been given his name.
He was kind to his parents and never arrogant.
He was the son of Zakariyya.
easy.explain: Allah gave Zakariyya the good news of a son "whose name is Yahya; We have given that name to none before him."

clues: He was a prophet sent to an Arab people.
His people carved homes out of the mountains.
They asked him for a miracle.
They killed the she-camel sent to them.
He was sent to Thamud.
easy.explain: Salih was sent to Thamud, who hewed houses in the mountains. They killed the she-camel of Allah and a mighty blast seized them.

clues: He was a prophet sent to an Arab people.
His people were tall and strong and built lofty buildings.
They boasted, "Who is mightier than us?"
They were destroyed by a furious wind.
He was sent to 'Ad.
easy.explain: Hud was sent to 'Ad, his brother in kinship. They rejected him and were destroyed by a roaring wind for seven nights and eight days.

clues: He was a prophet.
He is named in the Qur'an only twice.
He is described as truthful.
Allah says He raised him to a high place.
The Prophet ﷺ met him in the fourth heaven on the Mi'raj.
medium.explain: Allah says of Idris, "He was a man of truth, a prophet, and We raised him to a high station." In the Mi'raj hadith the Prophet ﷺ met him in the fourth heaven.

clues: He was a prophet.
His people cheated in weights and measures.
He told them, "Give full measure and weight."
His people were destroyed by an earthquake.
He was sent to Madyan.
medium.explain: Shu'ayb was sent to Madyan and warned them against giving short measure. They rejected him and the earthquake seized them.

clues: He was a prophet.
He is named in Surah Al-An'am and Surah As-Saffat.
His people worshipped an idol called Ba'l.
He asked them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
His name is often written Elias in English.
medium.explain: Ilyas told his people, "Will you call upon Ba'l and forsake the best of creators?"

clues: He was a prophet.
He is named in the Qur'an only twice.
He is named in Surah Sad.
He is listed among the chosen and the best.
His name is often written Elisha in English.
medium.explain: Allah says, "And remember Isma'il and Al-Yasa' and Dhul-Kifl, all are among the best."

clues: He is named in the Qur'an.
He is named twice, both times in a list.
He is described among the patient.
He is named next to Isma'il and Idris in Surah Al-Anbiya.
His name means "the one of the portion".
medium.explain: Allah says, "And Isma'il and Idris and Dhul-Kifl, all were among the patient."

clues: She was the wife of a prophet.
She was standing nearby when angels came as guests.
She laughed at the news she was given.
She was old when her son was born.
She was the mother of Ishaq.
medium.explain: Ibrahim's wife Sarah laughed when the angels gave her the good news of Ishaq, and after him Ya'qub.

clues: He was a relative of Khadijah.
He was an old man who had become blind.
He knew the earlier scriptures.
He said the angel who came to the Prophet ﷺ was the one sent to Musa.
Khadijah took the Prophet ﷺ to him after the first revelation.
medium.explain: Waraqah ibn Nawfal, Khadijah's cousin, told the Prophet ﷺ, "This is the same angel whom Allah sent to Musa."

clues: He came to Makkah as an enslaved boy.
He chose the Prophet ﷺ over going home with his own father.
He was freed and raised in the Prophet's household.
He was killed leading the army at Mu'tah.
He is the only companion named in the Qur'an.
medium.explain: Zayd ibn Harithah is the only companion named in the Qur'an, in Surah Al-Ahzab. He commanded the army at Mu'tah and was martyred there.

clues: He was a cousin of the Prophet ﷺ.
He led the Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia.
He spoke for them before the Negus.
He was martyred at Mu'tah.
He is remembered as the one with two wings in Paradise.
medium.explain: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, Ali's brother, was martyred at Mu'tah. Ibn Umar would greet his son as "son of the one with two wings".

clues: He came from a wealthy family in Makkah.
He gave up a life of comfort for Islam.
The Prophet ﷺ sent him to Yathrib to teach the Qur'an.
He carried the banner at Uhud and was killed there.
When he was buried, his cloak could not cover both his head and his feet.
medium.explain: Mus'ab ibn Umayr was martyred at Uhud. His shroud was too short: if his head was covered his feet showed, so they covered his feet with grass.

clues: He was among the earliest Muslims.
His whole family was tortured in Makkah.
His mother Sumayyah was the first martyr of Islam.
He helped build the mosque in Madinah, carrying two bricks at a time.
The Prophet ﷺ said the transgressing group would kill him.
medium.explain: While building the mosque, the Prophet ﷺ said of Ammar, "Alas for Ammar, the transgressing group will kill him."

clues: He came from Persia.
He travelled from teacher to teacher searching for the truth.
He was enslaved before reaching Madinah.
He is credited with suggesting the trench.
The Prophet ﷺ put his hand on him saying men of his people would reach faith even if it were at the Pleiades.
medium.explain: When Surah Al-Jumu'ah was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ put his hand on Salman and said that if faith were at the Pleiades, men from these people would reach it.

clues: He came from the tribe of Ghifar.
He travelled to Makkah to find out about the Prophet ﷺ.
He declared his Islam openly at the Ka'bah and was beaten for it.
He was known for his plain living.
His name is Jundub ibn Junadah.
medium.explain: Abu Dharr went to Makkah, accepted Islam and proclaimed it aloud near the Ka'bah, where the Quraysh beat him until al-Abbas protected him.

clues: He was one of the Ansar.
He accepted Islam as a young man.
He was known for his knowledge of halal and haram.
The Prophet ﷺ sent him to Yemen.
He was told to call the people first to the testimony of faith.
medium.explain: When sending Mu'adh to Yemen, the Prophet ﷺ told him to invite them first to testify that there is no god but Allah, then to the prayer, then to zakat.

clues: He was one of the Ansar.
He was a scribe of revelation.
He was among the best reciters of the Qur'an.
Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to recite a surah to him by name.
He wept when he heard that Allah had mentioned him.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ told Ubayy that Allah had commanded him to recite to him. Ubayy asked, "Did Allah name me?" and wept.

clues: He was one of the earliest Muslims.
He was short and thin.
He was a shepherd before Islam.
He recited the Qur'an aloud near the Ka'bah and was beaten for it.
The Prophet ﷺ asked him to recite to him, and wept at Surah An-Nisa.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ibn Mas'ud to recite to him. When he reached "How will it be when We bring from every nation a witness", the Prophet's eyes were full of tears.

clues: He was a cousin of the Prophet ﷺ.
He was still a boy when the Prophet ﷺ passed away.
He became a great scholar of the Qur'an.
The Prophet ﷺ prayed for Allah to teach him the Book.
He is often called the interpreter of the Qur'an.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ embraced Ibn Abbas and said, "O Allah, teach him the Book."

clues: He was one of the Ansar.
His mother brought him to the Prophet ﷺ as a boy.
He narrated very many hadith.
He lived a very long life.
He served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years.
medium.explain: Anas said, "I served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years, and he never said to me 'uff', nor asked why I did something or why I did not."

clues: He was a chief of the Aws.
His acceptance of Islam brought his whole clan into Islam.
He was wounded at the Battle of the Trench.
He judged the case of Banu Qurayzah.
The Prophet ﷺ said the Throne shook at his death.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "The Throne of the Most Merciful shook at the death of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

clues: He was one of the earliest Muslims.
He was one of the ten promised Paradise.
He commanded the Muslim armies in Syria.
He died of the plague of Amwas.
The Prophet ﷺ called him the trustworthy one of this ummah.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Every nation has a trustworthy one, and the trustworthy one of this ummah is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah."

clues: He was a cousin of the Prophet ﷺ.
His mother was Safiyyah, the Prophet's aunt.
He was one of the ten promised Paradise.
He married Asma bint Abi Bakr.
The Prophet ﷺ called him his disciple (hawari).
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Every prophet had a disciple, and my disciple is az-Zubayr."

clues: She was an early Muslim woman.
She was the daughter of a caliph.
She carried food to the cave during the Hijrah.
She tore her waistband in two to tie the provisions.
She is called the one with two waistbands.
medium.explain: Asma tore her waistband in two to tie up the food for the Hijrah, so she was named Dhat an-Nitaqayn, the one with two waistbands.

clues: She was one of the Prophet's wives.
Her first husband, a veteran of Badr, died in Madinah.
Her father offered her in marriage to Uthman and Abu Bakr first.
The written sheets of the Qur'an were kept with her.
She was the daughter of Umar.
medium.explain: After Abu Bakr and then Umar, the sheets of the Qur'an were kept with Hafsah. Uthman borrowed them to make the standard copies.

clues: She was one of the Prophet's wives.
She was his cousin.
She was previously married to Zayd ibn Harithah.
She would say Allah married her from above the seven heavens.
Her marriage is mentioned in Surah Al-Ahzab.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Ahzab says, "We married her to you." Zaynab used to say her family married the others, while Allah married her from above the seven heavens.

clues: He was one of the Ansar.
He was famous for his words.
He defended the Prophet ﷺ against the Quraysh.
The Prophet ﷺ prayed that Jibril would support him.
He was the poet of the Prophet ﷺ.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said to Hassan, "Answer on behalf of Allah's Messenger. O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit."

clues: He was blind.
He was one of the early Muslims of Makkah.
A surah opens by mentioning him.
He gave a second adhan at dawn in Madinah.
"He frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him."
medium.explain: Surah 'Abasa was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum. In Madinah he called the adhan for Fajr after Bilal's earlier call.

clues: He was a leader of Quraysh.
He was one of the fiercest enemies of the early Muslims.
He killed Sumayyah, the first martyr.
He led the Quraysh army at Badr.
Two young men of the Ansar struck him down at Badr.
medium.explain: At Badr, two young men of the Ansar, Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, struck Abu Jahl down.

clues: He was a ruler.
He received a letter from the Prophet ﷺ.
He questioned Abu Sufyan about the Prophet ﷺ.
He concluded that the Prophet's rule would reach the ground under his feet.
He was the emperor of Byzantium.
medium.explain: Heraclius questioned Abu Sufyan in detail about the Prophet ﷺ, as told in the long hadith at the start of Sahih al-Bukhari.

clues: He is named in the Qur'an.
He served a tyrant.
He was told to bake bricks of clay.
He was told to build a tower to look for the God of Musa.
He was the minister of Fir'awn.
medium.explain: Fir'awn said, "O Haman, kindle for me a fire on the clay and build me a tower, that I may look at the God of Musa."

clues: He was from the people of Musa.
He was extremely wealthy.
The keys to his treasures were heavy for a group of strong men.
He said his wealth came from his own knowledge.
The earth swallowed him and his house.
medium.explain: Qarun boasted that he was given his treasures because of his knowledge. Allah caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling.

clues: He is named once in the Qur'an.
He worshipped idols.
His son argued with him about them.
He threatened to stone his son.
He was the father of Ibrahim.
medium.explain: Ibrahim said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods? I see you and your people in clear error."

clues: He was a king of Bani Isra'il.
His people objected because he was not wealthy.
He was given knowledge and stature.
He tested his army at a river.
His army defeated Jalut.
medium.explain: Allah appointed Talut (Saul) as king. He tested his soldiers at a river and led the few who passed against Jalut.

clues: He led an army against Bani Isra'il.
His army was larger than theirs.
The believers prayed for patience before facing him.
He is often called Goliath in English.
Dawud killed him.
medium.explain: Allah says, "And Dawud slew Jalut, and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom."

clues: He lived among Bani Isra'il.
He led many of them astray while Musa was away.
He said he took a handful of dust from the messenger's tracks.
He was told he would say "Do not touch me" all his life.
He made the golden calf.
medium.explain: Musa asked al-Samiri what he had done. He made the calf from the people's ornaments, and his punishment was to say "No touching" for the rest of his life.

clues: They are two angels.
They are named in Surah Al-Baqarah.
They were sent down in Babylon.
They taught nothing without first warning, "We are only a trial."
People learned from them what causes division between husband and wife.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Baqarah says the two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut, taught no one without saying, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve."

clues: He is an angel.
He is named once in the Qur'an.
The people of the Fire will call out to him.
They will ask him to let his Lord end their lives.
He is the keeper of Hell.
medium.explain: The people of the Fire will cry, "O Malik, let your Lord make an end of us!" He will say, "You will remain." Some translations, like Pickthall, render the name as "master".

clues: He is an angel.
He is not named in the Qur'an.
The Prophet ﷺ named him in his night prayer.
He is mentioned there with Jibril and Mika'il.
He is commonly known as the angel who will blow the Trumpet.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ began his night prayer with, "O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil."

clues: They are angels.
They are with every person.
They never miss anything.
They write down what people do.
Their name means "the noble scribes".
medium.explain: Allah says, "Indeed over you are guardians, noble, recording; they know whatever you do."

clues: The Prophet ﷺ reached it on the Mi'raj.
It is mentioned in Surah An-Najm.
The Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril there in his true form.
The Garden of Refuge is near it.
It is a lote tree.
medium.explain: Surah An-Najm says the Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril "by the lote tree of the utmost boundary, near which is the Garden of Refuge."

clues: It is a house.
It is in the heavens.
Allah swears by it in Surah At-Tur.
Seventy thousand angels enter it every day and never return.
Its name means "the much-frequented house".
medium.explain: In the Mi'raj hadith, the Prophet ﷺ was shown al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, which seventy thousand angels enter every day.

clues: It is mentioned in the Qur'an.
Nothing in it can be changed.
Everything that will happen is written in it.
The Qur'an is recorded in it.
Its name means "the Preserved Tablet".
medium.explain: Surah Al-Buruj says, "Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an, in a Preserved Tablet."

clues: It is the greatest of created things.
Angels carry it.
Eight angels will bear it on the Day of Judgement.
Al-Firdaws lies beneath it.
Allah rose over it, in a way that befits Him.
medium.explain: The Qur'an calls Allah the Lord of the Mighty Throne, and says eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that day.

clues: It is mentioned in the Qur'an.
It grows in the depths of Hell.
Its fruit is like the heads of devils.
The people of the Fire will eat from it.
It is a tree.
medium.explain: Surah As-Saffat describes the tree of Zaqqum that grows in the heart of Hell, its fruit like the heads of devils.

clues: It is mentioned in the Qur'an.
It is in Paradise.
Its drink is mixed with ginger.
It is named in Surah Al-Insan.
It is a spring.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Insan describes a cup mixed with ginger from a spring there called Salsabil.

clues: It is mentioned in the Qur'an.
It is in Paradise.
Those brought near to Allah drink from it.
It is named in Surah Al-Mutaffifin.
It is a spring.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mutaffifin says the drink of the righteous is mixed with Tasnim, a spring from which those brought near drink.

clues: It is a place in the Hereafter.
It lies between Paradise and Hell.
Men on it recognise everyone by their marks.
They hope to enter Paradise.
A whole surah is named after it.
medium.explain: Surah Al-A'raf describes a partition between the people of Paradise and Hell, and on the heights are men who know each group by their marks.

clues: It is a voluntary prayer.
It has two rak'ahs followed by a supplication.
The Prophet ﷺ taught it the way he taught a surah.
It is prayed before making a decision.
Its name means "asking for what is best".
medium.explain: Jabir said the Prophet ﷺ taught them istikharah in all matters as he taught them a surah of the Qur'an.

clues: It is an act that wipes something out.
It is required after certain sins or broken oaths.
Feeding ten poor people is one form of it.
Fasting three days is another option for an oath.
Its name means "expiation".
medium.explain: Surah Al-Ma'idah gives the expiation for a broken oath: feeding ten poor people, clothing them, or freeing a slave, and if not possible, fasting three days.

clues: It is a period of time.
It follows a divorce or the death of a husband.
A woman does not remarry during it.
Its length differs from case to case.
For a widow it is four months and ten days.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Baqarah says widows wait four months and ten days. Surah At-Talaq tells men to divorce at the beginning of the waiting period and count it.

clues: It is connected to money.
It is forbidden in Islam.
Allah declares war on those who will not give it up.
The Qur'an contrasts it with trade, which is lawful.
It means interest or usury.
medium.explain: Allah says, "Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury." Those who persist are warned of war from Allah and His Messenger.

clues: It is a principle of community life.
It is praised among the qualities of the believers.
The Prophet ﷺ was told to practise it with his companions.
Umar left the choice of caliph to six men using it.
It means mutual consultation.
medium.explain: The Qur'an praises those whose affairs are decided by consultation, and tells the Prophet ﷺ to consult them in the matter.

clues: It is a single prostration.
It can happen outside the prayer.
It is connected to the Qur'an.
The Prophet ﷺ made it at the end of Surah An-Najm.
It is made when reciting certain verses.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ recited Surah An-Najm and prostrated, and those with him prostrated too.

clues: It is a concession in the prayer.
It is for the traveller.
It is mentioned in Surah An-Nisa.
It applies to the prayers of four rak'ahs.
It means shortening the prayer.
medium.explain: Allah says, "When you travel in the land, there is no sin on you if you shorten the prayer." Four-rak'ah prayers are prayed as two.
